proof_scope: At actual T=1 and tau=7/50, two zero-threshold pinned reflections have limiting signed-test limsup less than -0.01212878 for each sign on all sufficiently large eligible primes. This uses an Arb compact limiting integral plus a norm bound for the unknown transformed first threshold. It tolerates total nonnegative threshold at most .01 and vanishing canonical mean or mark perturbations.

At the same T and tau, complementary theta ensures an interior feasible completion for at least one sign. Iterating the actual pinned reflections at threshold 1/2000 produces a nonnegative row in some sign within O(n) reflections. The sign is not specified in advance and simultaneous positivity is open.

For the true time-averaged rows, add a mark-zero anchored row and apply one reflection. The sufficient scaled mean increment is at most 2 n^(1/4) times the corresponding opposite projected terminal difference norm divided by T. It is O(sqrt(n)/T) uniformly for floors in [0,1], so this gives explicit simultaneous completion at any T much larger than sqrt(n). The known short marked-cancellation window does not reach this horizon.

For the true stationary curve, the variational envelope gives the first 2J signed scalar coefficients from J directional Hessian jets and an explicit square norm defect at order 2J+1. A finite Bang inequality permits field-first fixed-order quasi-analytic derivative bounds to propagate actual hot decay. The real test allows marked ramification.

On actual squares the hot and cold data force violation of these derivative envelopes in finite blocks above any fixed starting order, both for supremum and integrated derivative tests. The prime-uniform scalar derivative envelopes remain unproved.

For an even subgroup B of nonzero squares, the signed shifted coset fiber second moment over opposite cells is exactly (q-S^2)/2, with S the twisted character sum. A near-critical twist forces almost two-to-one fibers outside the (+,+) cells with an explicit parity law for collisions. Positive linear-in-p odd-cell counts would exclude this twisted single-coset obstruction through primes. Finite exact records show the square norm-one subgroup has zero odd cells; no all-prime count or general critical-support gap is proved.
